items.title: OpenAI invites brands to set up shop in ChatGPT
items.content:
Read Online | Sign Up | Advertise

Good morning, {{ first_name | AI enthusiasts }}, and welcome to our 5,653 new readers. Google conditioned companies to obsess over their search listings for decades. That same scramble has been playing out on AI platforms, and OpenAI just gave brands an official way in.

Its new ‘Businesses’ beta gives brands a verified profile, a view of their mentions, and a personalized AI agent for direct buyer questions, opening a new way to meet customers where they’re increasingly searching… inside ChatGPT.

In today’s AI rundown:

  • OpenAI invites brands to set up shop in ChatGPT

  • Anthropic stretches Claude across the office

  • Put your open Chrome tabs to work with AI

  • ‘AI 2027’ authors move up their timelines

LATEST DEVELOPMENTS

OPENAI

🛒 OpenAI invites brands to set up shop in ChatGPT

Image source: OpenAI

The Rundown: OpenAI just introduced Businesses in ChatGPT, a beta hub where brands can claim a verified profile, track how often the chatbot mentions them, and set up AI agents for shoppers, which paid ads can now point to.

The details:

  • Profiles are currently free to claim for eligible companies, while agents are live first for U.S. online retailers and digital service firms.

  • Brands can write their agent’s instructions and add product details, with shoppers opening it from the profile in a labeled chat separate from ChatGPT’s answers.

  • A dashboard shows how often ChatGPT mentions a brand and drives clicks to its site, plus “discovery topics” that can point to gaps in what the brand shares.

  • OpenAI first piloted ad-linked agents in September, and brands can now pay to make their agent the landing spot for ads in ChatGPT, with each paid spot labeled.

Why it matters: Brands used to fight for a spot in Google’s results, and in the AI era, that’s shifted to getting name-dropped by the assistants themselves. Companies were mostly guessing what ChatGPT said about them or paying outside specialists to find out. OAI just handed them that visibility directly, plus a one-on-one line to potential customers right inside the chat.

TOGETHER WITH MEMOKET

🗓️ Your conversations, now in Apple Calendar

The Rundown: Memoket Gem is an AI wristband that captures conversations with one press and turns them into summaries, action items, and connected memory. Now with Apple Calendar integration: connect in the Memoket iPhone app to automatically sync new recordings as calendar events.

With Memoket, you can:

  • Find recordings by when the conversation happened

  • Revisit decisions and context across conversations

  • Bring relevant memories into ChatGPT and Claude

  • Use the app on your Apple Watch, coming this month

Discover Memoket Gem.

ANTHROPIC

🗄️ Anthropic stretches Claude across the office

Image source: Anthropic

The Rundown: Anthropic just rolled out Claude Sheets and Whiteboards in beta — spreadsheets and shared boards Claude builds alongside a team — while making its Claude Data analytics tool generally available and announcing Claude Meetings, an assistant that sits in on video calls.

The details:

  • Sheets can build a working spreadsheet with formulas via prompt and export it to Excel, while Whiteboards maps a plan onto a shared board for a team to edit.

  • Claude Data, originally named Dashboards when it entered beta in October, turns company metrics into narrated videos and visual data stories.

  • Product lead Nicholas Lin said Claude joins nearly every Anthropic meeting after months of testing, with a Google Meet beta coming to Team and Enterprise users.

  • Upgraded connectors, the links between Claude and other work apps, now also open tools like Adobe and Atlassian fully inside Claude without switching platforms.

Why it matters: Claude continues to eat both legacy office software and the newer apps that followed, with spreadsheets, dashboards, and meeting tools now joining Slides, Design, and Docs. The apps it hasn’t rebuilt now open inside Claude anyway, pulling more use into the AI assistant and away from the tools the workday used to run on.

AI TRAINING

🌐 Put your open Chrome tabs to work with AI

The Rundown: In this guide, you’ll use ChatGPT’s updated Chrome extension to compare open pages, check the facts, and group the tabs you need. Start in Chat to read, then use Work for a browser action you approve.

Step-by-step:

  1. Install the official ChatGPT extension from OpenAI and open its side panel. Use a practice Chrome profile with public pages for your first run

  2. Open three pricing pages and tell ChatGPT which tabs to read. Give it your team size, required features, budget, and billing period

  3. Check the comparison against the pages. Confirm the full team cost and leave missing details unverified rather than guessing

  4. Switch to Work where available and ask it to group only those three tabs. Review the list first, then check the actual group in Chrome

  5. Ask for a short recommendation with source links and one question to resolve. Keep trials, purchases, and messages outside the task

Pro tip: Use the same side panel on any article. Select the tab and ask ChatGPT for the main claim, the evidence, and what the author leaves unresolved.

PRESENTED BY GARTNER

🎰 Only 1 in 5 AI use cases pays off  

The Rundown: Enterprise AI use cases grew by 400% this year, but not all are delivering ROI. Investment without value only creates bad momentum. These Gartner IT Symposium/Xpo takeaways show what separates mere AI activity from real, measurable results.

What you’ll learn:

  • How to build momentum that compounds value

  • Ways to prevent key risks

  • How to make people your AI safety net

Download the insights.

AI RESEARCH

📆 ‘AI 2027’ authors move up their timelines

Image source: AI Futures Project

The Rundown: The AI Futures Project, the forecasting group behind AI 2027, just moved up its forecast for AI that matches the best human AI researchers up to 2027 — citing AI evaluator METR’s recent outside review of Anthropic’s AI speedup as its biggest reason.

The details:

  • The group’s paper published in 2025 depicted AI rapidly improving itself, but most of the authors later pushed their dates for AI that beats top experts into the 2030s.

  • METR estimated Anthropic now improves about 2x as fast, mostly thanks to AI, a pace the forecasters’ models gave under 4% odds of seeing this early.

  • Ex-OpenAI researcher Daniel Kokotajlo gave the earliest date, a 50-50 chance by May 2027, while the other five forecasters land between August and November.

  • Kokotajlo wrote on X that he is “scared, sad, and angry,” and the group says that if its forecast holds, a pause “should be the top priority for the AI industry.”

Why it matters: AI 2027 is considered one of the more prescient forecasts for how the industry has accelerated, and even its own authors said the pace shown in METR’s report caught them off guard. If their updated projections are as accurate as their old ones, the industry has months, not years, to prepare for the implications of superhuman AI research capabilities.

QUICK HITS

COMMUNITY AI WORKFLOW OF THE DAY

▸ Polly built a caregiver recordkeeping app with Claude

Today’s workflow comes from reader Polly Bouker:

“My son is disabled and receives state funding for caregiving. The program requires daily records of what was done, whether he met his goals, and any behavioral or health issues. A program coordinator reviews these periodically, and an auditor may review them too. I used Claude to write the code for a web app built with Google tools that handles this recordkeeping.

Each day, caregivers open the app and check off each item on my son’s daily task list, which he completes with their help. The app writes the required daily summary from those check-offs and adds goal tracking. Everything goes into a printable report for the coordinator or an auditor.

My son has his own view showing how much of his list is checked off and how close he is to his favorite reward. Because he is motivated to see that he has earned the reward, he reminds the caregivers to complete their part.”

📰 Everything else in AI today

Triple Whale’s 50 LLM Prompts to Crush BFCM 2026 turns your data into answers with copy-paste prompts for any LLM: 35 to plan, 10 to run live all weekend, 5 to save soft results.*

Anthropic opened the investor pitch for its IPO coming next week, also saying in an updated filing that it now considers its AI R&D capability threshold met, based on what it expects from upcoming models.

Adobe previewed MCP connector tools that let users’ own AI agents edit Photoshop, Illustrator, and Premiere files coming in early 2027, plus Firefly Graph, a beta builder for repeatable, shareable AI workflows.

France unveiled the Paris Call for AI Safety and Security, with signers such as OAI, Anthropic, and Mistral committing to build emergency off switches into their most advanced models.

items.title: Anthropic says ‘pacing, not pausing’ with Fable 5.2
items.content:
Read Online | Sign Up | Advertise

Good morning, {{ first_name | AI enthusiasts }}, and welcome to our 5,334 new readers. Anthropic spent the fall telling the AI industry to pace itself. The company’s first look at what that means just arrived, and the result still sits comfortably at the top of the leaderboards.

Fable 5.2 is cheaper, faster, and strong enough to bump Google’s Gemini 4 Carbon before the public even got to try it. If this is Anthropic’s slow lane, it still looks faster than the rest of the industry can keep up with.

In today’s AI rundown:

  • Anthropic’s Fable 5.2 leads the frontier with a price cut

  • Meta undercuts Anthropic, OpenAI on the cost of agents

  • Clean up a messy Excel report with Claude

  • Google adds two more AI chips to its Nvidia fight

LATEST DEVELOPMENTS

ANTHROPIC

🧠 Anthropic’s Fable 5.2 leads the frontier with a price cut

Image source: Artificial Analysis

The Rundown: Anthropic just released Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, two cheaper, faster upgrades to its most powerful AI family that take the top spot on Artificial Analysis’ AI leaderboard — and show how CEO Dario Amodei’s call to “pace the frontier” will work.

The details:

  • Fable debuted at No. 1 on Artificial Analysis’ Intelligence Index leaderboard, edging out Google’s still unreleased Gemini 4 Carbon model by 5 points.

  • Mythos is limited to vetted security and life sciences groups, while Fable is the same model with stronger cyber and biology guardrails.

  • Teams of 1,000 Fable agents built an operating system in 8 days and formalized the full proof of a famous math problem in 30 hours, with Opus finishing just 26%.

  • Fable was held near Opus level in certain skills that speed up development, with exec Dianne Penn saying of the slowdown, “We called for pacing, not pausing.”

  • 5.2 is 20% cheaper and as much as 30% faster than 5.1, though at $8 in / $40 out per million tokens, it still costs twice as much as Opus 5.5.

Why it matters: Google’s run at the top of the leaderboard ended before Carbon was even released, and Anthropic’s pacing certainly doesn’t feel like a slowdown for users without its internal super-models. With OpenAI also expected to release a new model, the bar just moved even higher — and anything less will likely come as a disappointment.

TOGETHER WITH VANTA

🚀 Governance at the speed of AI

The Rundown: Vanta’s AI governance webinar series is six live and on-demand sessions for security and GRC leaders on how to govern AI as fast as you adopt it — covering frameworks, expert Q&A, AI risk, and a live product demo.

In the series, you’ll explore:

  • Frameworks for governing AI from day one

  • Real-time Q&A with Vanta’s GRC experts

  • AI risk, workshops, and a live demo

Register for a session.

META

🔥 Meta undercuts Anthropic, OpenAI on the cost of agents

Image source: Meta

The Rundown: Meta released Muse Ember, the smallest AI model in its lineup, built to handle routine, high-volume steps inside AI agents — with the company saying it matches Anthropic’s budget Claude Haiku 5.5 at roughly one-third of the per-task cost.

The details:

  • Ember tied Haiku 5.5 at 36 on AA’s Intelligence Index, while beating out OpenAI’s comparable GPT-6 Luna (28) by a wide margin.

  • Meta AI chief Alexandr Wang said Ember is meant to pair with the larger Muse Wonder, writing that “wonder can plan, ember can handle the volume.”

  • Ember’s price matches both rivals, with savings coming from using fewer tokens per job and an average test task running $0.14 on Ember and $0.41 on Haiku.

  • Meta trained Ember using its larger Muse Wonder Full, the first model built that way, and said “even more efficient models” are in training.

Why it matters: Meta shipped its first Muse model in April, and it now has answers for every tier Anthropic and OpenAI sell, from the near-frontier down to the bargain bin. Add in a new report of a sales push through the consulting giants those two already use, and Meta’s 2026 consumer success might soon touch the enterprise end of the AI pool.

AI TRAINING

📊 Clean up a messy Excel report with Claude

The Rundown: In this guide, you’ll use Claude inside Excel to clean up a messy sales export, fix a wrong total, and build a report. You’ll check the numbers and test whether a new order updates the chart.

Step-by-step:

  1. Install the official Claude add-in and open a copy of your workbook. Pro members can use our practice file and keep the reference workbook closed until they finish

  2. Tell Claude what each row means and which orders to count. Ask it to find duplicate rows, missing details, and formula mistakes before changing anything

  3. Approve the fixes on a separate sheet. Keep the original data and ask for a record of each change, including any rows left out

  4. Build a monthly report with formulas and a chart. Check the order count, refunds, and sales total against the source rows

  5. Add a test order and check that the report and chart update. Remove it and confirm the original totals return before saving your finished workbook

Pro tip: A spreadsheet can show a wrong total without showing an error. Ask Claude to explain which rows it counted, then check a few yourself.

PRESENTED BY CUBE.DEV

🧠 How BetterUp gets trusted AI answers with Cube

The Rundown: Cube is the semantic layer for AI. Define metrics and access rules once, let AI build your model, and agents, dashboards and apps get consistent answers. BetterUp’s team uses it to query governed data right in Claude, saying it delivers “reliable results, even if you don’t know exactly the right question to ask.”

With Cube, you can:

  • Model metrics and joins in code, with access policies enforced at query time

  • Connect Claude or ChatGPT over MCP to chat with your governed data

  • Build dashboards without code: a non-technical BetterUp manager built one of its most-used dashboards

See BetterUp’s story, then get started with no card required.

GOOGLE

💾 Google adds two more AI chips to its Nvidia fight

Image source: Google

The Rundown: Google announced the TPU 8tx and 8i Max, two specialized versions of its custom AI chips arriving next year, with one built to keep sensitive data safe and the other to handle jobs needing an AI to hold huge amounts of information at once.

The details:

  • Google began selling TPUs to other companies this year and has nearly 100 customers, including Anthropic and Apple, with every available chip spoken for.

  • Data stays encrypted on the 8tx even while an AI model is working on it, a step where it normally sits exposed, with governments and regulated firms as targets.

  • The 8i Max joins two chips as one unit to double processing power and memory speed, for AI agents that must keep an entire codebase or long video in view.

  • “The future is going to be about specialization,” Amin Vahdat, who runs Google’s chip work, told Bloomberg, expecting both to reach customers next year.

Why it matters: Google couldn’t have asked for better timing, rolling out two Nvidia challengers the day after Jensen Huang’s apology and his board’s probe. While Google still seems constrained in how much it can build, the demand is clearly there — making it interesting both as a chip supplier and as an AI lab that owns its entire stack.

QUICK HITS

COMMUNITY AI WORKFLOW OF THE DAY

▸ A Rundown reader built an AI running coach for a friend

Today’s workflow comes from an anonymous Rundown reader:

“My friend is a competitive runner who wears a Garmin watch for every session. Each run produces a spreadsheet’s worth of data: pace, heart rate, cadence, ground contact time, vertical oscillation, and power, broken down lap by lap. Garmin Connect shows the numbers but can't explain them. It can't tell him whether a late pace drop came from fatigue, wind, or a hill, or whether his fitness is really improving. I built Stride to add that meaning for runners who already have the data.

Stride runs sports-science-style analysis. Aerobic fitness tracks heart rate within each pace band week over week, so a lower heart rate at the same pace signals improving fitness. The Environment layer adds weather and elevation, so a slow lap into a headwind is judged fairly.

AI Coach sends a structured 30-day summary to Claude, which returns a plain-English brief on trends, environmental factors, and things to watch. What-If answers questions grounded in his own data, such as his likely 5K time on a flat, windless course.”

See the workflow on our Community Workflow Hub →

How do you use AI? Tell us for a chance to be featured in the newsletter.

🛠️ Trending AI Tools

  • 🏆 Claude Fable 5.2 - Anthropic’s top-ranked model for the hardest challenges

  • 🎨 Seedream 5.5 - ByteDance’s new image AI with strong editing skills

  • 🔥 Muse Ember - Meta’s low-cost AI model for coding and agent tasks

  • 🖋️ Inkling 2 Small - Thinking Machines Lab’s new coding and vision model

📰 Everything else in AI today

Nvidia’s top lawyer reportedly emailed agents in August 2025 as they investigated whether Singapore’s Megaspeed smuggled its chips to China, with the U.S. Commerce Department then halting the case and handing it to the Justice Department.

Anthropic is preparing to proceed with its IPO despite current fear in the AI sector, with shares likely launching for trading as soon as Thursday next week, The WSJ reports.

Adobe signed a multi-year deal with Disney to build custom models trained on Disney’s characters and visual styles, with work underway for theme parks, film, and ESPN.

Instagram launched Effect Builder, a free web tool that lets U.S. users turn text prompts into AI Stories effects, which others can use after passing a safety review.

items.title: Jensen Huang admits affair amid spy claims
items.content:
Read Online | Sign Up | Advertise

Good morning, {{ first_name | AI enthusiasts }}, and welcome to our 9,830 new readers. A week ago, Nvidia was brushing off a report about an alleged spy plot involving its CEO as routine customer meetings. Now, Jensen Huang is publicly apologizing, and his own board is investigating.

Few founders are as inseparable from what they built as Huang, and no company touches the entire global AI industry like Nvidia. So the fallout from his admitted affair could reach far beyond a single boardroom.

In today’s AI rundown:

  • Jensen Huang admits affair as Nvidia probes spy claims

  • The Rundown Roundtable: Our AI use cases

  • Turn your X bookmarks into a personal research desk

  • Anthropic’s Claude ‘dreams’ to fix its own memory

LATEST DEVELOPMENTS

NVIDIA

🕵️ Jensen Huang admits affair as Nvidia probes spy claims

Image source: NetThunder on LinkedIn

The Rundown: Nvidia’s board of directors just ordered an independent review of reports that CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by a “foreign intelligence effort,” with Huang admitting to an extramarital affair in a letter to staff and saying, “There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.”

The details:

  • Sec. of State Marco Rubio reportedly oversaw a spring memo on Jensen and Alice Huang, an Nvidia customer exec it linked to China’s top spy agency.

  • After calling their meetings “completely normal” last month, Jensen told staff, “I was unfaithful to my wife” and reportedly confirmed the relationship to the board.

  • Reporting has yet to establish what, if anything, Ms. Huang (aka Huang Le, no relation to Jensen) learned from him, while China denies the spying claims.

  • Outside lawyers and independent directors will run the review as Jensen stays CEO, with the board seeing “no reason to believe” any secrets were compromised.

  • Jensen also has until Nov. 11 to answer a House GOP request for a private briefing, with more congressional investigations expected over the relationship.

Why it matters: AI stocks are already reeling from the midterm election results. Now, a spy scandal around the CEO of one of the industry’s biggest companies is unlikely to help either. Nvidia touches nearly every aspect of the AI industry, and Huang is the frontman of it all, so all eyes will be on what the board finds and his future with Nvidia.

TOGETHER WITH GARTNER

🔮 How can you predict IT workforce needs? 

The Rundown: AI is accelerating how fast skills become obsolete, making future workforce needs nearly impossible to predict. This Gartner webinar explores three planning traps and offers a framework for building a resilient IT workforce.

In this webinar, you'll learn how to:

  • Avoid common workforce planning traps

  • Separate enduring from transient skills

  • Align talent with long-term value

Register today.

THE RUNDOWN ROUNDTABLE

💡 The Rundown Roundtable: Our AI use cases

The Rundown: The Rundown Roundtable is a weekly feature where we poll members of The Rundown staff about how we use AI in our work and daily lives.

Brooke, Community Lead: I'm on the customer side, not the engineering side. When something breaks, I usually find out when a customer writes in, and by then a bunch of people have already hit it. We had an error chart in our analytics tool, but I don't often remember to check that dashboard every day, and a basic “alert me over X errors” setup would go off constantly for things that aren't real problems.

I built a Claude scheduled task that checks our error chart every morning, filters out the noise, and tells the whole team in Slack only when something's actually wrong. I set it up just by describing what I wanted in plain English. I gave Claude the rules on which error types are real problems and which aren't, and it only counts the ones that matter.

Now, I hear about issues before customers have to tell me. I tested it over the past couple of weeks, and it flagged every day something really broke and stayed silent on a busy day that was all harmless errors.

Jennifer, Tech & Robotics Writer: My preteen daughter has spent months debating whether or not to get bangs, mostly worried about the "total humiliation" if they went wrong. So we uploaded her photo to ChatGPT and asked for four versions of bangs: blunt, curtain, wispy, side-swept.

She loved it and finally narrowed down her choice, and the appointment is booked for this weekend. It’s hardly a groundbreaking use case, but it’s a fun way to try on a decision before a stylist makes it permanent.

AI TRAINING

🔖 Turn your X bookmarks into a personal research desk

The Rundown: X moves quickly, and saving posts is easy. Finding the useful ideas again is harder. In this guide, you’ll connect Grok Bot to X, review a week of bookmarks, spot repeated themes, and turn one finding into a post draft.

Step-by-step:

  1. Check the difference between free Grok chat and Grok Bot. Bot is included with Premium, Super, and Ultra on the X Subscription. X Chat is still rolling out

  2. Connect the official X plugin with the Grok Bot. Check that it is linked to the same account where you save posts

  3. Bookmark 8 to 12 useful posts about one topic. Choose examples, questions, and problems, not just launch announcements

  4. Message your Bot in X Chat and ask it to group the bookmarks into themes. Check the direct links and compare each claim with the original post

  5. Choose one supported theme and ask for an X post draft. Review the wording and sources yourself; leave publishing off

Pro tip: A set of bookmarks can show what you have been reading, but it can’t prove what all of X thinks. Keep the source links with every theme.

PRESENTED BY OPENART

💡 Create a launch video for your business

The Rundown: Need a launch video for your business? Simply paste your website link, add your brand assets, and define your target audience. OpenArt's AI video agent will shape the story and messaging while handling the script, motion design, voiceover, and video editing.

With OpenArt, you can:

  • Turn your website, screenshots, or pitch deck into a launch video

  • Create short promos or longer videos to showcase your business

  • Refine scenes, voiceovers, or music by describing the changes

  • Go beyond launches with product ads and UGC-style videos

Create your launch video with OpenArt.

ANTHROPIC

💤 Anthropic’s Claude ‘dreams’ to fix its own memory

Image source: Anthropic

The Rundown: Anthropic just published its own take on AI “dreaming,” sharing how Claude agents use downtime to fix and reorganize their memory, and what it’s learned about what an AI should actually bother remembering.

The details:

  • Memory refers to notes Claude saves as files and reads back in later sessions, so it can build on past work instead of starting from scratch each time.

  • Unlike ChatGPT’s version, which previously built a profile of the user, Anthropic’s dreaming has Claude check its notes against logs of past work to catch errors.

  • Anthropic said newer models have gotten much better at judging what to save, and that explaining to the AI why memory matters beats rules on what to write.

  • In tests on Pokémon, Fable 5 earned four badges with only 10 memory files, while an older Sonnet 3.7 got just one using 413, and Opus 5.5 beat the game entirely.

Why it matters: It feels like not too long ago that the early iterations of ‘memory’ in AI assistants were a comically simple scratchpad with bare-bones notes on the user. Now they can recall past chats in detail down to the most obscure reference, and the next step is agents that continuously remember the job and improve at it the longer they work.

QUICK HITS

COMMUNITY AI WORKFLOW OF THE DAY

▸ Kate built a custom camera feature for Facebook Live presentations

Today’s workflow comes from reader Kate MacGregor:

“I built a live camera bubble that floats over my slides during Facebook Live presentations. Because Facebook Live does not let me switch between my camera and a shared screen, I wanted my face to stay visible while I presented. This is useful for anyone who streams presentations to a Facebook Group and wants viewers to see them speaking.

Claude Code built the working app within about five minutes. I made one tweak to the camera bubble's shape, and it was then a finished, usable product.

When I'm ready to go live in the Facebook Group, I click the camera bubble app on my local desktop. It uses my laptop camera, and I can drag the bubble around the screen and choose the circle size that suits whatever I'm sharing. Before I go live, I select "share entire screen" in the Facebook Live settings. Viewers then see my slides or screen with my floating camera bubble, so they can see me speaking as I present.”

items.content:

Good morning, {{ first_name | AI enthusiasts }}, and welcome to our 4,687 new readers. Anthropic has made “pacing the frontier” part of its pitch, holding back on what it hands the public. Inside the lab, the pace appears to be a different story.

After 11 weeks inside the lab’s data, METR estimates Anthropic’s progress has roughly doubled, with its own AI driving most of the jump and no clear bottlenecks to slow it down. When the public gets to see the models behind it is another question.

LATEST DEVELOPMENTS

ANTHROPIC

📈 METR’s inside look at Anthropic’s AI speedup

Image source: METR

The Rundown: AI-evaluation nonprofit METR just published a new report on its findings from 11 weeks of inside access to Anthropic’s internal data and interviews with staff, concluding the company’s AI progress is likely running about 2x as fast as before, mostly due to its own AI — though Anthropic redacted most of the strongest evidence.

The details:

  • METR’s estimated range of speedup over Anthropic’s 2024–25 pace runs from 1.3 to 3x, with METR crediting AI for around 80% of the company’s faster progress.

  • Anthropic co-founder and safety lead Sam McCandlish said the lab’s heavy redactions were to avoid “handing out a roadmap for others to go faster.”

  • The report also revealed two internal models ahead of its top-ranked Claude Opus 5.5, including a “Model 4” that cleared 50% on all 15 tested benchmarks.

  • Anthropic’s IPO filing defined a danger threshold as “dramatically accelerated progress attributable to AI,” with Monday’s update saying that point may be close.

Why it matters: METR’s own Ryan Greenblatt said he was “seriously wrong” after expecting a much slower speedup this year. AI helping build better AI is the loop every lab is chasing and every safety plan worries about, and it already seems to be running inside Anthropic. With METR spotting no clear bottlenecks, that loop may only get faster.

ROWAN’S CORNER

3️⃣ The ‘Three Times’ rule

Image source: The Rundown @ Google I/O

Rowan: I have a rule before I’m allowed to automate anything: I have to do it manually at least three times first.

Every automation I’ve shared here has followed it. I ran my Friday “factory inspections” by hand for months before handing them to an agent. I sorted my contacts and wrote my own follow-ups before my agents took those over. The manual reps were the training data for my own judgment.

When you do a task yourself a few times, you learn what good looks like, which steps actually matter, and where things tend to go wrong (that’s what also lets you check an agent’s work later instead of blindly trusting it).

It also fixes the most common mistake I see when people start building with AI, which is going into the tools looking for problems to solve. Flip it. Find the real problems in your life and work first, do them manually three times, then (and only then) automate them. The time you free up will surface the next problem, and then you repeat.

That loop is how real AI productivity happens. It’s never one tool automating everything at once; it’s an iterative process that stacks, and six months in you’re a different operator.

So before you build the agent, do the task yourself on Monday, again on Wednesday, and again on Friday. Then automate the version you actually understand.

AI TRAINING

💼 Use AI to find a job and prepare to get hired

The Rundown: In this guide, you’ll use AI to find real job openings, compare them with your experience, tailor your resume, and practice for an interview. One fictional applicant carries through the full process, so you can follow along before using your own details.

Step-by-step:

  1. Choose one target job title, two related titles, and your limits for location, work setup, salary, and experience.

  2. Ask ChatGPT to find five current openings. Check each role on the employer’s own careers page before adding it to your list.

  3. Compare one verified job description with a redacted copy of your resume. Ask AI to show strong matches, partial matches, and missing requirements.

  4. Tailor the resume and write a short cover letter using only facts you can support. Review every new claim before saving or applying.

  5. Practice eight interview questions, one at a time, then add the application and next follow-up date to your tracker.

Pro tip: Ask AI to show the evidence behind every resume change. A keyword is useful only when it describes work you’ve actually done.

OPENAI

🖼️ OpenAI’s Images 2.6 adds GIFs to ChatGPT

Image source: OpenAI

The Rundown: OpenAI just released Images 2.6, an upgraded, faster image model family rolling out across its ChatGPT and Codex platforms with new built-in GIF capabilities that can animate a typed idea, photo, or sketch.

The details:

  • OAI already held the top spot across image benchmarks with its previous models, and 2.6 edges just past its predecessor for No. 1 on Design Arena.

  • Two versions are available for developers via API, with Sunburst for higher-quality work and Flare for lighter, faster jobs.

  • 2.6 is the first OpenAI image model to add motion, able to convert existing images or ideas into moving GIFs or create entirely new animations from scratch.

  • Users can change a GIF’s speed or rework single frames, with the company saying the model also generates images 50% faster than previous versions.

Why it matters: Fun? Yes. The Astra 6.2 upgrade everyone wanted? No. OpenAI still leads in image generation, but with Anthropic topping the main AI leaderboards for months, anything short of the next major model release (widely expected this week) is an appetizer.
